question: Where is the human heart primarily located within the thoracic cavity?
explanation: The heart sits securely in the central part of the chest known as the middle mediastinum, positioned right between the two lungs. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T10#BMP111_U5_T10_h1)

question: Why is the pericardial fluid surrounding the heart so essential during daily life?

options.A: It pumps excess blood out of the thoracic cavity
options.B: It supplies oxygen directly to the heart muscle cells
options.C: It reduces friction as the heart beats against surrounding tissues
options.D: It cools down the body temperature during hard physical work

explanation: The serous fluid inside the pericardial sac acts as a lubricant, allowing the heart to move smoothly and painlessly with every contraction. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T10#BMP111_U5_T10_h1)

question: Which of the three heart wall layers is responsible for generating the pumping force?
explanation: The myocardium is made of thick, specialized cardiac muscle tissue that contracts forcefully to pump blood around the body. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T10#BMP111_U5_T10_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the endocardium inside the heart chambers?

options.A: It absorbs extra nutrients directly from the flowing blood
options.B: It produces the lubricating fluid found in the pericardial sac
options.C: It expands the chest cavity during heavy physical exercise
options.D: It provides a smooth surface to prevent abnormal blood clotting

explanation: The slick endothelial lining prevents blood cells from sticking and forming dangerous clots inside the active heart chambers. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T10#BMP111_U5_T10_h2)

question: Which heart chamber has the thickest muscular wall because it pumps blood to the entire systemic circulation?
explanation: The left ventricle needs a very thick, muscular wall to generate enough pressure to send blood through the whole body. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T10#BMP111_U5_T10_h3)

question: How do the functions of the atria differ fundamentally from the ventricles?

options.A: Atria have thick muscular walls while ventricles have very thin delicate walls
options.B: Atria pump blood to the lungs while ventricles pump blood to the brain
options.C: Atria hold oxygenated blood while ventricles hold only deoxygenated blood
options.D: Atria act as receiving chambers while ventricles act as discharge pumps

explanation: Blood returns from the body into the atria first, which then pass it down into the ventricles to be forcefully pumped out of the heart. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T10#BMP111_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is the specific name of the valve located between the left atrium and the left ventricle?
explanation: The mitral valve, also called the bicuspid valve, guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T10#BMP111_U5_T10_h4)

question: What exact purpose do the chordae tendineae serve during ventricular contraction?

options.A: They push the blood forcefully out through the semilunar valves
options.B: They supply the inner heart muscle fibers with fresh oxygenated blood
options.C: They anchor the atrioventricular valves to prevent them from flipping backward
options.D: They conduct electrical impulses from the atria down to the ventricles

explanation: The chordae tendineae hold the valve flaps firmly in place when the ventricles squeeze, stopping blood from leaking back up into the atria. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T10#BMP111_U5_T10_h4)

question: Where do the coronary arteries that supply the heart muscle originate?
explanation: The right and left coronary arteries branch directly off the base of the aorta just above the aortic semilunar valve. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T10#BMP111_U5_T10_h5)

question: Why can the myocardium not extract all the oxygen it needs directly from the blood inside its own chambers?

options.A: The heart beats too fast for oxygen to transfer through the inner lining
options.B: The blood inside the chambers is always completely devoid of any oxygen
options.C: The heart muscle walls are too thick for simple diffusion to reach every cell
options.D: The endocardium blocks all gas exchange between the chambers and the muscle

explanation: Because the myocardium is thick and dense, internal chamber blood cannot nourish the outer muscular layers, requiring a separate coronary blood supply. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T10#BMP111_U5_T10_h5)
